mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month period, the 5-day SPX forward return after such a rate hike is not statistically different from the 5-day return after a pre-hike rate hike (<0.05 t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) below the prior month's level, accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO), predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as a labor market softening dampens corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month AND INDPRO < previous month
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market weakening
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where the trigger occurs but SPX 20-day return is positive (>0.5%), with a p-value > 0.05 in a two-sample test versus baseline windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 10% year-over-year coincides with a rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL), signaling resilient demand and supporting a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY growth > 10% AND CPIAUCSL month-over-month > 0.3%
failure_condition: Over 5 such triggered windows, the 60-day SPX forward return is not statistically superior to the mean of non-triggered windows (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline of at least two consecutive months in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend implies supply-side softness, which predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < trend line for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 10 such contraction windows, the 5-day SPX forward return is not statistically negative (mean <= 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0% for the first time in three months, accompanied by a decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL), it signals a strong labor market that may prompt the Fed to hold rates steady, supporting a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: Labor market tightening with cooling inflation
failure_condition: In 10 such trigger windows, the 20-day SPX forward return is not statistically positive (mean <= 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly rise in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual: a sustained decline in UNRATE below 5.0% for three months suggests labor market tightness, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days when combined with GDP growth proxies like GDPC1 trend growth.
regime_hint: Labor market tightness in a growth cycle
failure_condition: Over 5 such windows, the 60-day SPX forward return is not statistically higher than the mean of non-triggered windows (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time monthly drop in retail sales proxy (assumed proxy: HOUST) of more than 5% accompanied by a rise in consumer confidence (not directly observable, but as a counterfactual: a negative surprise in CPIAUCSL) predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to risk-off sentiment.
failure_condition: In 10 such triggered windows, the 20-day SPX forward return is not significantly negative (mean <= 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A long-term upward trend in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) of at least 2% per year is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days due to higher expected cost pass-through and equity valuation adjustments.
failure_condition: Over 15 consecutive 60-day windows with CPIAUCSL annualized > 2%, the 60-day SPX forward return is not statistically positive (mean <= 0, p > 0.05).
